statement: Given \(c > 0\), a sequence \((x_n)\) is defined by \(x_{n+1} = \sqrt{c - \sqrt{c + x_n}}\) for \(n \geq 0\). Find all values of \(c\) such that for each initial value \(x_0 \in (0, c)\), the sequence is defined for all \(n\) and has a finite limit as \(n \to +\infty\).

Two circles \((O_1)\) and \((O_2)\) are given. Let \(M_1, M_2\) be points on \((O_1), (O_2)\) respectively, and let lines \(O_1M_1\) and \(O_2M_2\) meet at \(Q\). Starting simultaneously, \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) move clockwise on their circles with the same angular velocity.
a) Determine the locus of the midpoint of \(M_1M_2\).
b) Prove that the circumcircle of \(\triangle M_1QM_2\) passes through a fixed point.

Consider \(P(x) = x^3 + 153x^2 - 111x + 38\).
a) Prove that there are at least nine integers \(a \in [1, 3^{2000}]\) for which \(3^{2000} \mid P(a)\).
b) Find the exact number of integers \(a \in [1, 3^{2000}]\) with the property from (a).

For every integer \(n \geq 3\) and angle \(\alpha\) with \(0 < \alpha < \pi\), let \(P_n(x) = x^n \sin\alpha - x\sin n\alpha + \sin(n-1)\alpha\).
a) Prove there is a unique polynomial \(f(x) = x^2 + ax + b\) dividing \(P_n(x)\) for every \(n \geq 3\).
b) Prove there is no polynomial \(g(x) = x + c\) dividing \(P_n(x)\) for every \(n \geq 3\).
Find all integers \(n \geq 3\) such that there exist \(n\) points in space, with no three collinear and no four concyclic, such that all circles through any three of the points are congruent.
Let \(P(x)\) be a nonzero polynomial such that \(P(x^2-1) = P(x)P(-x)\) for all real \(x\). Determine the maximum possible number of real roots of \(P(x)\).
